## Overview `FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4` sends sparse MQA prefill to FlashInfer's trtllm-gen kernel, one query at a time. This PR runs it on FA4 instead: 2, 4 or 8 consecutive queries of a request share each 128-head kernel row (the grouped mode of vllm-project/flash-attention#205), and a new Triton kernel builds each group's top-k union. Depends on vllm-project/flash-attention#205: while this is a draft, `cmake/external_projects/vllm_flash_attn.cmake` points at that PR's commit. Related PRs: #48726 (LiteDSA, under review) groups neighbouring queries in the same way for the FP8 sparse MLA path, with its own SM100 kernel in the FlashInfer sparse backend, and also covers 8 heads per rank; the reviewer has asked for it to be split into separate PRs. This PR is a smaller, BF16-only change confined to the FA4 sparse MLA backend: it reuses FA4's MLA kernel through vllm-project/flash-attention#205, and the two PRs touch no common files. The same idea is merged in SGLang for SM90 and SM120 (sgl-project/sglang#32779). This PR builds on #55866 (FA4 sparse MQA decode) and leaves the masked-MHA routing from #53785 as is. ## Claims - **Sparse MQA prefill is 1.37-1.55x faster end to end** on `nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4` (TP4, B300, BF16 KV). With default routing this covers pure prefills above the masked-MHA threshold (48K tokens: 2.59 → 1.72 s) and prefills on cached context (1.42-1.43x); shorter pure prefills use masked MHA and are unchanged. - **No accuracy loss:** with every prefill forced through the new path, GSM8K 5-shot goes from 93.63% to 93.86% (± 0.67), and perplexity over 46K teacher-forced tokens does not change. - Decode, and the configurations grouping does not cover (DCP, PCP, HiSparse, heads per rank other than 16, 32 or 64), keep their current kernels. ## Validation All runs: B300, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (8e2beaa3b), with this branch's three changed Python files and the three changed `cute` files of flash-attention#205 bind-mounted. The nightly's copies of those six files are otherwise identical to this branch's base (f46ea25e) and to flash-attention b273a02 (the current pin). I did not build this branch from source. **Tests** ```bash pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k 'query_group or fa4 or sparse_backend_decode_correctness' # 396 passed, 1350 skipped, 151 deselected in 1337s ``` - `test_build_query_group_union_matches_reference`: the Triton union against a Python reference, including an empty group, `block_stride_rows > block_size` and chunked groups. - `test_fa4_sparse_grouped_prefill_correctness[16, 32, 64 heads]`: a decode request plus two prefills whose lengths leave tails, run through two layers of one index group and compared with an fp32 reference. It checks that both prefills ran grouped on both layers, that each union was built once and reused by the second layer, and that a head-major `q_nope` (as the DSA model produces) works. The grouped test needs SM100 and an FA build that includes flash-attention#205, so CI covers it once the pin includes that PR. **End-to-end prefill latency.** Baseline nightly on GPUs 0-3 and this PR on GPUs 4-7 of one machine, with: ```bash vllm serve nvidia/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --served-model-name glm52 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --max-model-len 65536 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 65536 --max-num-seqs 16 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA_SPARSE_FA4 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --enable-prefix-caching # right column: both servers with --attention-config '{"sparse_mla_force_mqa": true}' python3 e2e_prefill.py --urls http://127.0.0.1:8400 http://127.0.0.1:8500 --out r.json ``` Each request asks for one token on public-domain text (Project Gutenberg #1342 and #2701). I didn't compare greedy outputs because the baseline is not run-to-run deterministic on prompts longer than the top-k (2,048 tokens): the same prompt sent twice with different `cache_salt` diverges after 5-30 generated tokens. Agreement between the servers is a little below each server's run-to-run agreement, as expected from two kernels that round differently (their outputs differ by about one BF16 ulp, see flash-attention#205); perplexity does not move. **Union build cost**, one prefill request on a B300, synthetic top-k with unions of 1.9K-2.7K rows (GLM-5.2 measured 2.3K-3.2K), median of 20 calls (`bench_union_build.py`): | Tokens | 8K | 16K | 32K | 48K | |---|---|---|---|---| | Per index group | 0.16 ms | 0.31 ms | 0.76 ms | 1.55 ms | | GLM-5.2 forward (21 of 78 layers build it) | 3.4 ms (1.3%) | 6.5 ms (1.3%) | 15.9 ms (1.5%) | 32.5 ms (1.9%) | Percentages are of this PR's forced-MQA prefill latency above. The tables above predate the branch's last change, a one-line guard that keeps PCP on the existing path. tuple[float, int]: body = {"model": "glm52", "prompt": prompt, "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0} req = urllib.request.Request(f"{url}/v1/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) t0 = time.perf_counter() with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r: usage = json.load(r)["usage"] return time.perf_counter() - t0, usage["prompt_tokens"] def main() -> None: ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--urls", nargs="+", required=True) ap.add_argument("--pure", type=int, nargs="*", default=[8192, 16384, 32768, 49152]) ap.add_argument("--context", type=int, nargs=2, action="append", default=None, metavar=("CACHED", "NEW"), help="cached prefix tokens and new tokens") ap.add_argument("--trials", type=int, default=3) ap.add_argument("--salt", default=secrets.token_hex(8)) ap.add_argument("--out", required=True) args = ap.parse_args() contexts = args.context if args.context is not None else [[16384, 8192], [24576, 8192]] text, cursor = load_text(), 0 print(f"salt {args.salt}", flush=True) def take(tokens: int, salted: bool) -> str: nonlocal cursor n = int(tokens * CHARS_PER_TOKEN) if cursor + n > len(text): cursor = 0 s = text[cursor : cursor + n] cursor += n return f"[{args.salt}]\n{s}" if salted else s results = [] cases = [("pure", n, 0) for n in args.pure] + [("context", new, cached) for cached, new in contexts] for kind, new, cached in cases: runs = {u: [] for u in args.urls} tokens = {} for trial in range(args.trials): prefix = take(cached, salted=True) if cached else "" body = take(new, salted=not cached) order = args.urls if trial % 2 == 0 else args.urls[::-1] for u in order: if cached: complete(u, prefix) # warm the prefix cache, not timed dt, n_tok = complete(u, q) for p, q in zip(x["logprobs"], y["logprobs"])] agree += sum(p == q for p, q in zip(x["top1"], y["top1"])) n += len(x["logprobs"]) sa += sum(x["logprobs"]); sb += sum(y["logprobs"]) da.sort() print(f"{n} positions | mean |dlogprob| {sum(da) / n:.5f}, p99 {da[int(0.99 * n)]:.4f}, max {da[-1]:.4f} | " f"top-1 agreement {agree / n:.4%} | perplexity {math.exp(-sa / n):.4f} vs {math.exp(-sb / n):.4f}") if __name__ == "__main__": ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--base-url") ap.add_argument("--model", default="glm52") ap.add_argument("--cache-salt", default="r1") ap.add_argument("--out") ap.add_argument("--compare", nargs=2) a = ap.parse_args() if a.compare: compare(*(json.load(open(f)) for f in a.compare)) else: json.dump(probe(a.base_url, a.model, a.cache_salt), open(a.out, "w")) ``` ```python """Time build_query_group_union for one prefill request: N queries, top-k 2048, groups of 8. ## Details **Why.** FA4's sparse MLA kernel needs 128 query heads per KV head. Under tensor parallelism DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x have 16-64 heads per rank, so this backend runs prefill on trtllm-gen one query at a time, and each query streams its own 2,048 KV rows. Consecutive queries select mostly the same rows, though: on GLM-5.2 the union of 8 consecutive queries' top-k is 1.2-1.7x the size of one list. flash-attention#205 lets each 128-head row hold `128 / heads` queries that gather their union once, with a membership mask per query; at 16 heads it is 4.0x faster than trtllm-gen on GLM-5.2's top-k. **Changes** - `sparse_utils.build_query_group_union` (Triton, two kernels): for one request, marks each group's selected positions in a byte-per-position bitmap (bit t for query t), then emits the union in position order, mapped to KV rows through the request's block table, as `row | membership << 24`, -1 padded to a whole 128-entry tile, plus the union length per group. - `FlashAttnMLASparseFA4Impl._forward_mqa_kernel`: for prefill, the first `n // G * G` queries of each request run grouped; the last `n % G`, decode rows and padding rows run on the one-query-per-row FA4 kernel this backend already uses for decode. Prefill stays on trtllm-gen when the heads per rank are not 16, 32 or 64, under DCP or PCP, with HiSparse, when decode needs an LSE, or when the cache has 2^24 - 1 or more KV rows. - The union depends only on the logical top-k and the block table, which an index group shares, so the group's first layer builds it and the others reuse it (`_query_group_unions`). - `_forward_mqa_kernel` doesn't receive the metadata, so `forward_mqa` keeps it on the impl for the duration of the call. - `flash_attn_varlen_func` passes `gather_kv_query_group_size` through (default 1, no change). **Tradeoffs and limitations** - **Query copy.** The DSA model's absorbed `q_nope` is head-major (`bmm(...).transpose(0, 1)`), while grouping needs token-major rows, so the grouped rows are copied (tokens × heads × 512 BF16). Producing a token-major `q_nope` in the model would remove the copy. - **Union build scaling.** Each group scans a bitmap as long as the request, so the cost grows with prefill length × sequence length: 1.9% of the prefill at 48K. A sort-based union would avoid that if longer contexts need it. - **Low overlap.** When consecutive queries' top-k barely overlap, grouping is slower than one query per row: break-even is near a union of 5.8 lists per group of 8, while GLM-5.2's unions are 1.2-1.7 lists (flash-attention#205). - **First call compiles.** The grouped kernel is compiled on first use. Under default routing, the first grouped prefill of a process took ~4 s longer (5.95 s vs 1.73 s at 48K). With forced MQA, the startup dummy runs already compile it. vLLM's JIT warmup doesn't cover FA4's top-k paths yet (see the TODO in `v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/flash_attn.py`). - **Routing.** With this PR, MQA prefill also beats masked MHA from 8K to 32K (0.266 vs 0.346 s at 7.9K, 1.065 vs 1.474 s at 31.2K), so the FA4 entries of `_MASKED_MHA_THRESHOLDS` could move down. That changes a routing policy, so I'd propose it separately. - **KV dtype.** BF16 KV only, like the rest of this backend. AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and the benchmarks, which ran on my machine; I reviewed every changed line. This stays a draft until flash-attention#205 is merged and the cmake pin points back at vllm-project/flash-attention. ---

headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) t0 = time.perf_counter() with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r: usage = json.load(r)["usage"] return time.perf_counter() - t0, usage["prompt_tokens"] def main() -> None: ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--urls", nargs="+", required=True) ap.add_argument("--pure", type=int, nargs="*", default=[8192, 16384, 32768, 49152]) ap.add_argument("--context", type=int, nargs=2, action="append", default=None, metavar=("CACHED", "NEW"), help="cached prefix tokens and new tokens") ap.add_argument("--trials", cursor + n > len(text): cursor = 0 s = text[cursor : cursor + n] cursor += n return f"[{args.salt}]\n{s}" if salted else s results = [] cases = [("pure", n, 0) for n in args.pure] + [("context", new, cached) for cached, new in contexts] for kind, new, cached in cases: runs = {u: [] for u in args.urls} tokens = {} for trial in range(args.trials): prefix = take(cached, salted=True) if cached else "" body = take(new, salted=not cached) order = args.urls if trial % 2 == 0 else args.urls[::-1] for u in order: if cached: complete(u, prefix) # warm the prefix cache, not timed dt, n_tok = complete(u, prefix + body) runs[u].append(dt) tokens[u] = n_tok row = {"kind": kind, "cached_tokens": cached, "new_tokens": new, "prompt_tokens": tokens, "latency_s": {u: [round(x, 4) for x in v] for u, v in runs.items()}, "median_s": {u: round(statistics.median(v), 4) for u, v in runs.items()}} base, other = args.urls[0], args.urls[-1] row["speedup"] = round(row["median_s"][base] / q) for p, q in zip(x["logprobs"], y["logprobs"])] agree += sum(p == q for p, q in zip(x["top1"], y["top1"])) n += len(x["logprobs"]) sa += sum(x["logprobs"]); sb += sum(y["logprobs"]) da.sort() print(f"{n} positions | mean |dlogprob| {sum(da) / n:.5f}, p99 {da[int(0.99 * n)]:.4f}, max {da[-1]:.4f} | " f"top-1 agreement {agree / n:.4%} | perplexity {math.exp(-sa / n):.4f} vs {math.exp(-sb / n):.4f}") if __name__ == "__main__": ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--base-url") ap.add_argument("--model", default="glm52") ap.add_argument("--cache-salt", default="r1") ap.add_argument("--out") ap.add_argument("--compare", nargs=2) a = ap.parse_args() if a.compare: compare(*(json.load(open(f)) for f in a.compare)) else: json.dump(probe(a.base_url, a.model, a.cache_salt), open(a.out, "w")) ``` ```python """Time build_query_group_union for one prefill request: N queries, top-k 2048, groups of 8. ## Details **Why.** FA4's sparse MLA kernel needs 128 query heads per KV head. Under tensor parallelism DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.x have 16-64 heads per rank, so this backend runs prefill on trtllm-gen one query at a time, and each query streams its own 2,048 KV rows. Consecutive queries select mostly the same rows, though: on GLM-5.2 the union of 8 consecutive queries' top-k is 1.2-1.7x the size of one list. flash-attention#205 lets each 128-head row hold `128 / heads` queries that gather their union once, with a membership mask per query; at 16 heads it is 4.0x faster than trtllm-gen on GLM-5.2's top-k. **Changes** - `sparse_utils.build_query_group_union` (Triton, two kernels): for one request, marks each group's selected positions in a byte-per-position bitmap (bit t for query t), then emits the union in position order, mapped to KV rows through the request's block table, as `row | membership << 24`, -1 padded to a whole 128-entry tile, plus the union length per group. - `FlashAttnMLASparseFA4Impl._forward_mqa_kernel`: for prefill, the first `n // G * G` queries of each request run grouped; the last `n % G`, decode rows and padding rows run on the one-query-per-row FA4 kernel this backend already uses for decode. Prefill stays on trtllm-gen when the heads per rank are not 16, 32 or 64, under DCP or PCP, with HiSparse, when decode needs an LSE, or when the cache has 2^24 - 1 or more KV rows. - The union depends only on the logical top-k and the block table, which an index group shares, so the group's first layer builds it and the others reuse it (`_query_group_unions`). - `_forward_mqa_kernel` doesn't receive the metadata, so `forward_mqa` keeps it on the impl for the duration of the call. - `flash_attn_varlen_func` passes `gather_kv_query_group_size` through (default 1, no change). **Tradeoffs and limitations** - **Query copy.** The DSA model's absorbed `q_nope` is head-major (`bmm(...).transpose(0, 1)`), while grouping needs token-major rows, so the grouped rows are copied (tokens × heads × 512 BF16). Producing a token-major `q_nope` in the model would remove the copy. - **Union build scaling.** Each group scans a bitmap as long as the request, so the cost grows with prefill length × sequence length: 1.9% of the prefill at 48K. A sort-based union would avoid that if longer contexts need it. - **Low overlap.** When consecutive queries' top-k barely overlap, grouping is slower than one query per row: break-even is near a union of 5.8 lists per group of 8, while GLM-5.2's unions are 1.2-1.7 lists (flash-attention#205). - **First call compiles.** The grouped kernel is compiled on first use. Under default routing, the first grouped prefill of a process took ~4 s longer (5.95 s vs 1.73 s at 48K). With forced MQA, the startup dummy runs already compile it. vLLM's JIT warmup doesn't cover FA4's top-k paths yet (see the TODO in `v1/attention/backends/mla/prefill/flash_attn.py`). - **Routing.** With this PR, MQA prefill also beats masked MHA from 8K to 32K (0.266 vs 0.346 s at 7.9K, 1.065 vs 1.474 s at 31.2K), so the FA4 entries of `_MASKED_MHA_THRESHOLDS` could move down. That changes a routing policy, so I'd propose it separately. - **KV dtype.** BF16 KV only, like the rest of this backend. AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change, its tests and the benchmarks, which ran on my machine; I reviewed every changed line. This stays a draft until flash-attention#205 is merged and the cmake pin points back at vllm-project/flash-attention. ---
